title: Refine an etale fibre product to a Cartesian closed pair
statement:
Let $S,X,M_1,M_2$ be affine schemes, let $i_a:X\hookrightarrow M_a$ be closed immersions, and let $e_a:M_a\to S$ satisfy $e_1i_1=e_2i_2$. Suppose $e_2$ is etale. Put $P=M_1\times_SM_2$, with projections $p_a$, and let $s:X\to P$ be the map $(i_1,i_2)$. For every $x\in X$ there is an open neighbourhood $U\subset P$ containing $s(X)$ such that $p_1|_U$ is etale and
$$U\times_{M_1}X=s(X)$$
scheme-theoretically, with the identification induced by $s$. If $e_1$ also is etale, $U$ can be chosen so that $p_2|_U$ is etale and also $U\times_{M_2}X=s(X)$. The point $s(x)$ has residue field canonically equal to $\kappa(x)$. More precisely, $F_1=P\times_{M_1}X\to X$ is separated etale and $s$ induces an open-and-closed section in $F_1$; its complement is closed in $P$, and $U$ can be obtained by deleting it. In the two-etale case delete the analogous closed complement in $F_2=P\times_{M_2}X$ as well. All the displayed identifications are compatible with the given maps from $X$. Closed immersions, etaleness, separatedness, base change and residue fields have the meanings of [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-base-change], [def-weil-residue-field]; affine schemes are spectra of commutative rings [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Construct s = pullback.lift i1 i2 h and t1 = pullback.lift s (identity X) using s followed by p1 = i1. The two pullback projection equations give t1 followed by j1 = s and t1 followed by q1 = identity X. No iterated-fibre-product comparison is needed.

source.place: Fibre-product universal property; etale.tex Tag 024T, section/graph construction

proof.text: The projection p1 is etale by base change of e2; q1 is etale by base change of p1. The projection j1 is a closed immersion by base change of i1. Mathlib infers separatedness of q1 using its affine/pullback separatedness instances: affine schemes are separated, every map with separated source is separated, and separatedness is preserved by base change. These are the affine-source separatedness and closed-diagonal pullback arguments in the plan.

source.place: Tags 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion; schemes.tex Tags 01KN and 01KV. Separated base change is the displayed diagonal pullback.

proof.text: Apply the clopen-section theorem to the separated etale map $q_1$ and its section $t_1$. It identifies $X$ isomorphically with an open-and-closed subscheme $A_1=t_1(X)\subset F_1$, with inverse $q_1|_{A_1}$. Put $C_1=|F_1|\setminus|A_1|$. This is closed in $F_1$. Since $j_1$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset of $P$, the image $j_1(C_1)$ is closed in $P$ and disjoint from $s(X)$.

source.place: Tag 024T, proposition-properties-sections (3), followed by elementary closed-subspace topology

proof.text: Define U1 as the open complement of j1(F1 \ range(t1)). Injectivity of the closed immersion j1 gives j1^(-1)(U1) = range(t1), and the graph projection equation gives s(X) contained in U1. Factor s through U1 by IsOpenImmersion.lift. Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.isPullback proves the square with t1, this factorization, j1 and U1 inclusion is Cartesian from the equality of open inverse images. Paste it vertically with the defining pullback square for F1 and use t1 followed by q1 = identity X. This proves the required Cartesian square as schemes, retaining nilpotents.

source.place: Agent complement-removal consequence of Tag 024T; equality of open restrictions, not replacement by reduced closed subschemes

proof.text: The open inclusion $U_1\hookrightarrow P$ is etale and its composite with the etale map $p_1$ is etale, by the open-immersion and composition clauses. Consequently $U=U_1$ has every required property in the one-etale case.

If $e_1$ is etale as well, exchange the two indices in Steps 1--4. Now $F_2=P\times_{M_2}X\cong M_1\times_SX$, its map to $X$ is separated etale because $M_1$ is affine and $e_1$ is etale, and $t_2=(i_1,1_X)$ is its clopen section. Deleting its complementary closed subset in $P$ gives $U_2$ with $U_2\times_{M_2}X\cong X$ induced by $s$. Take $U=U_1\cap U_2$. Since $s(X)$ lies in both opens, restricting either of the previous Cartesian identifications to $U$ still gives all of $X$ with the same scheme structure. Both $p_a|_U$ are etale: each $p_a$ is a base change of the other $e_b$, followed by restriction to the open $U$. This also spells out the specified deletion of both closed complements.

source.place: Tag 024T with indices exchanged; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO, 01QR, 02GP, 02GN. Intersection and restriction are elementary.

proof.text: The factorization s = t1 followed by j1 is surjective on stalks, since open immersions and closed immersions are surjective on stalks. At x, each residue class in kappa(x) has a stalk representative, which lifts along the surjective stalk map of s; its residue class maps to the original one by ResidueField.map_residue. Thus the canonical residue-field map is surjective. It is injective as a homomorphism of fields, hence an isomorphism. Both Cartesian squares are pasted using the original graph maps, so all projection identities are compatible with i1 and i2. No nonempty or reduced hypotheses are used.

(2) p_1 and q_1 are base changes of e_2, so etale; j_1 is the base change of i_1, so a closed immersion; e_2 is separated because M_2 is affine, and the diagonal of q_1 is the pullback of the diagonal of e_2, which is correct. (6) In the two-etale case the intersection U_1 ∩ U_2 still pulls back to A_1 because s(X) lies in U_2. (7) A surjective local map gives an isomorphism of residue fields. Small cases tested: empty X; t ↦ t^2 from G_m to A^1 with X a point, which removes -1; nonreduced X; e_1 not etale. lean.statement: theorem etale_fibre_product_pair_refinement (S X M₁ M₂ : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine M₁] [IsAffine M₂] (i₁ : X ⟶ M₁) (i₂ : X ⟶ M₂) [IsClosedImmersion i₁] [IsClosedImmersion i₂] (e₁ : M₁ ⟶ S) (e₂ : M₂ ⟶ S) (h : i₁ ≫ e₁ = i₂ ≫ e₂) [Etale e₂] : ∃ (s : X ⟶ pullback e₁ e₂) (t₁ : X ⟶ pullback (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁), s = pullback.lift i₁ i₂ h ∧ t₁ ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁ = s ∧ t₁ ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁ = 𝟙 X ∧ Etale (pullback.snd (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁) ∧ IsSeparated (pullback.snd (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁) ∧ IsOpenImmersion t₁ ∧ IsClosedImmersion t₁ ∧ IsClosed ((pullback.fst (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁) '' (Set.range t₁)ᶜ) ∧ (∀ x : X, IsIso (s.residueFieldMap x)) ∧ ∃ (U₁ : (pullback e₁ e₂).Opens) (s₁ : X ⟶ U₁.toScheme), (U₁ : Set (pullback e₁ e₂ : Scheme.{u})) = ((pullback.fst (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁) '' (Set.range t₁)ᶜ)ᶜ ∧ (∀ x : X, s x ∈ U₁) ∧ s₁ ≫ U₁.ι = s ∧ Etale (U₁.ι ≫ pullback.fst e₁ e₂) ∧ IsPullback s₁ (𝟙 X) (U₁.ι ≫ pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁ ∧ (Etale e₁ → ∃ (t₂ : X ⟶ pullback (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂), t₂ ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂ = s ∧ t₂ ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂ = 𝟙 X ∧ Etale (pullback.snd (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂) ∧ IsSeparated (pullback.snd (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂) ∧ IsOpenImmersion t₂ ∧ IsClosedImmersion t₂ ∧ IsClosed ((pullback.fst (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂) '' (Set.range t₂)ᶜ) ∧ ∃ (U : (pullback e₁ e₂).Opens) (sU : X ⟶ U.toScheme), (U : Set (pullback e₁ e₂ : Scheme.{u})) = (((pullback.fst (pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁) '' (Set.range t₁)ᶜ) ∪ ((pullback.fst (pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂) '' (Set.range t₂)ᶜ))ᶜ ∧ (∀ x : X, s x ∈ U) ∧ sU ≫ U.ι = s ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ pullback.fst e₁ e₂) ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ pullback.snd e₁ e₂) ∧ IsPullback sU (𝟙 X) (U.ι ≫ pullback.fst e₁ e₂) i₁ ∧ IsPullback sU (𝟙 X) (U.ι ≫ pullback.snd e₁ e₂) i₂)
